subject: Clarify micro-call billing: atomicization, rounding, and contract floor
messages:
From: Taylor Morgan <taylor@novaretail.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15 09:12 -0700
Subject: Question on micro-calls and billing rounding

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — NovaRetail is excited about Redwood's latency and prefix cache savings. Before we move the procurement docs forward, the legal/finance team flagged a potential mismatch in how very short calls (what we call ‘micro-calls’ — single-field lookups, very short completions) are billed. A few specifics:

- Typical payload: 1–3 prompt tokens, model returns ~5–20 tokens.
- Volume: 40k–200k such micro-calls/day in peak flows, with many calls under 32 tokens.

Questions:
1) Do you bill strictly per-token (fractional) or do you round up to a quantum (e.g., 8-token minimum)?
2) If calls reuse prefixes or leverage KV cache, how is that credited?
3) Is there a contract-level minimum or monthly floor that would disproportionately affect these micro-calls?

We want to model expected spend for the POC. If you can share a short sample invoice calculation or simple rule-set, that would help our finance team.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

—Taylor
Procurement, NovaRetail
[Attachment referenced: NovaRetail_ROI_workflow.png (image/png)]

From: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Morgan <taylor@novaretail.com>
Date: 2028-03-15 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on micro-calls and billing rounding

Taylor — thanks for the clear examples, that helps. Short answers, then a few proposed rules and a request for one example flow so we can run numbers: 

1) Billing quantum: our public docs default to per-token metering but we apply a billing quantum for small calls to avoid extremely fine-grained line noise. Concretely: we round up to the nearest 8-token quantum per model call by default (this is our metering quantum for micro-calls).

2) Prefix/KV cache: when the prefix is present on the server and reused across calls, we apply a reuse credit. For repeated prefixes in the same conversation or session we do not re-bill identical prompt tokens; only the delta (new tokens) are billed after KV reconciliation.

3) Contract floor: standard enterprise contracts include a minimum monthly commitment (we can negotiate for pilots). That commitment is independent of per-call rounding; credits are applied towards the floor.

Proposed: if you can share one representative flow (CSV is fine) with prompt length, average completion length, and daily call volume, we’ll return a sample month projection and two commercial options:
A) Standard metering (8-token quantum, standard floor)
B) Pilot concession: temporary relaxation (first 90 days) where we bill at 50% of the quantum for calls under 64 tokens and apply no floor enforcement for pilot credits up to X dollars.

I’m attaching a short examples CSV and a one-pager on how prefix credits are computed. If that looks good I’ll loop Vanessa for the commercial side and Karthik for the implementation details.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: metering-examples.csv (text/csv)]

From: Taylor Morgan <taylor@novaretail.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-17 08:27 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on micro-calls and billing rounding

Soojin — thanks, the rules help. I attached a small sample (3 flows) we use internally. A couple follow-ups:

- For option B, can you confirm if the 50% quantum is a discount on the rounded-up amount or if you literally bill at 4-token quantum for those calls? Finance cares about the determinism of the invoice line items.
- How do you handle bursts where a single consumer does many micro-calls in short timeframe — does batching at the runtime level affect billing?

We’re hoping to keep predictability high for the pilot team; if you can put a simple sample invoice row for one of the flows (e.g., flow A: 120k calls/month, avg 18 tokens billed per call after prefix credit) that would go straight to our finance folks.

—Taylor
[Attachment: nova_sample_flows.csv (text/csv)]

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Morgan <taylor@novaretail.com>
Cc: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-20 09:09 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on micro-calls and billing rounding — pilot concession proposal

Hi Taylor — looping in Karthik for technical confirmation but wanted to put a commercial proposal on the table quickly.

Proposal (pilot, 90 days):
- Metering quantum: Redwood will apply an 8-token quantum as described. For calls <64 tokens we will bill at 50% of the quantum for the pilot (effectively treating an 8-token quantum as 4 tokens for invoice calculation only).
- Prefix credit: full prefix reuse credit as described by Soojin.
- Pilot cap: Redwood will cap pilot billable at $18,000/month (we’ll issue credits if usage exceeds that, up to cap).
- Post-pilot: revert to standard quantum and apply any contracted floor. We can bake a gradated discount if you sign a 12-month committed capacity.

Karthik — can you confirm no runtime-side changes are required and whether batching at runtime will cause any unexpected invoice skew if we apply the 50% pilot quantum?

Thanks — Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Commercial — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: NovaRetail_MA-terms_v3.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Morgan <taylor@novaretail.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-23 16:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on micro-calls and billing rounding — pilot concession proposal

Taylor — quick summary after internal confirm:

- Tech confirm (from Karthik): the pilot concession (bill at 50% of the 8-token quantum for calls under 64 tokens) is purely a billing-layer transform — no runtime code change required. Runtime batching will continue to operate for latency/cost efficiencies; we reconcile billing per logical call after batching and apply the pilot quantum transform at invoice time.

- Example invoice row (Flow A, your sample):
  • Calls: 120,000/month
  • Raw billed tokens per call (post-prefix credit): 18 tokens
  • Default quantum billing: round up to 24 tokens (nearest 8) => 120k * 24 = 2,880,000 tokens billed
  • Pilot concession: calls <64 tokens billed at 50% of quantum => treat 8-token quantum as 4 tokens for invoicing => 120k * 12 (=18 tokens * 0.666? see below) — to avoid ambiguity we will compute as: invoice_tokens = sum(min(raw_billed_tokens, 64) rounded to 8 * 0.5 + max(0, raw_billed_tokens - 64) rounded to 8)
  • In your Flow A case this yields an invoiced token count of ~1,440,000 tokens for the pilot month (we’ll provide line-by-line CSV).

- Pilot cap: we will cap your pilot invoiced amount at $18,000/month. Any excess will be issued as a credit (per Vanessa’s note).

Next steps: I’ll circulate the line-level sample invoice (CSV) for your finance team and a one-page clause to add to the pilot appendix confirming the invoicing transform and cap. If that looks good, we can attach it to the MA and proceed.

Thanks — looking forward,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pilot-invoice-sample.csv (text/csv)]
